source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi A,

Thanks for the update; the extra time is not a problem. Please remember, though, that while this is the inaugural issue dated November 1st, it must be released before that date.

Many thanks!

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
This is very disappointing. This was the only time we had to launch; anything later is too late, and on Friday you can't send out a communication.

So it's safe to say that we cannot launch a November 1st inaugural issue, because that falls on a Sunday. Everything will therefore have to be changed for December, which is not good.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I understand, and I am VERY humble and nice. Still, I can't allow that to cause a project to fail.

Whether a project is completed as agreed has nothing to do with its price or perceived value. This is a November issue, so it cannot launch later. Once you accept a project, you must ensure you have enough time to finish it, using as little or as much effort as necessary; otherwise, the whole thing becomes a waste for everyone.

The remark wasn't callous either. If a freelancer says the stated scope is inaccurate, that has to be confirmed. The print portion really was included in the original scope, and I removed it specifically to reduce the pressure.

I'm pleased with the work. The deadline is the only difficult part for both you and me—that's it, and I'm not complaining about anything else.
